Bitcoin Cash was launched in 2017 as the result of a Bitcoin hard fork. While it uses similar underlying code, there are some modifications, such as larger block sizes.\n\nAs a separate project from Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash has its own development teams and community.

Launched in 2009, Bitcoin is the original cryptocurrency. It was developed by an anonymous developer who uses the pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto.\n\nBitcoin relies on a decentralized network called a blockchain, which enables direct, peer-to-peer transactions.

Ethereum was created by computer programmer Vitalik Buterin and launched in 2015.\n\nThe Ethereum blockchain network introduced the concept of smart contracts and paved the way for a diverse array of decentralized applications, or dApps, to flourish. Ethereum, also known as ETH or Ether, is the native cryptocurrency powering the network. There is no cap on the total supply of ETH.

LINK is the native cryptocurrency token of the Chainlink network, used to incentivize node operators who retrieve and verify external data, and as payment for these oracle services.\n\nChainlink, launched in 2019, is a decentralized oracle network that helps smart contracts securely connect with real-world data, APIs, and traditional financial systems. It\'s crucial for blockchain apps that need off-chain information to work effectively.

Litecoin was created in 2011 from a fork in the Bitcoin blockchain.\n\nAs its name suggests, it shares codebase details with Bitcoin, but its network operates under different rules. Litecoin has decreased block processing time—2.5 minutes on average compared to Bitcoin\'s 10 minutes—and typically has lower transaction fees for users transacting directly on the Litecoin network.

Polygon is a platform that supports the Ethereum blockchain and helps it serve more users as it grows. MATIC is Polygon\'s currency and it\'s used to pay for transactions on the Polygon network. Polygon supercharges Ethereum, allowing it to process more transactions.
